text:
Inclusive education aims to ensure that students with different abilities, needs, and backgrounds can participate meaningfully in learning. Artificial intelligence can support this objective by providing tools that improve accessibility and adapt educational content. At the same time, poorly designed technology may create new barriers.

AI-powered accessibility tools can assist students with disabilities. Speech-to-text systems may help students who have difficulty typing, while text-to-speech applications can support learners with visual impairments or reading difficulties. Real-time captions may also improve access for students with hearing loss. These technologies can increase independence and reduce reliance on constant individual assistance.

Adaptive learning systems may further support students who require different levels of difficulty or alternative explanations. For example, a learner with attention difficulties may benefit from shorter tasks and frequent feedback, while another student may require visual examples instead of long written instructions.

However, accessibility depends on design quality. Speech recognition systems may perform poorly with certain accents, speech conditions, or background noise. Visual interfaces may also be difficult to navigate for students using assistive technologies. When AI tools are developed without testing them with diverse users, they may exclude the very students they are intended to support.

Privacy is another concern. Inclusive learning systems may collect sensitive information about disabilities, learning difficulties, or behavioural patterns. Schools must protect this data and limit its use to legitimate educational purposes.

AI can make education more inclusive by removing barriers and adapting learning materials to individual needs. However, technology must be designed with accessibility, privacy, and user diversity in mind. Inclusion requires more than adding AI tools; it requires involving students and educators in decisions about how those tools are developed and used.
